meta.title: x/tools/gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: slicescontains offers fix that elides an implicit interface conversion
meta.fix_ref: golang/tools@51dcb32d9b95 (gopls/internal/analysis/modernize: add checks to prevent invalid fixes from slicesContains; CL 669355)
meta.build_notes: Both built and run with go1.24.4 (golang.org/dl, under temp/lsp_servers/go-sdks; toolchain.json): the local go1.27 cannot build v0.18.1, go1.24.0 (current when v0.18.1 was tagged, 2025-02-24) cannot build v0.19.0 (its go.mod requires go >= 1.24.2), and go1.24.4 was the current Go release when v0.19.0 was tagged (2025-06-10). The fix merged 2025-05-08.
meta.notes: The slicescontains pass rewrote a loop that calls cb(fruit), with cb func(FruitInfo) bool and fruit of the concrete type Fruit, to slices.ContainsFunc(fruits, cb), which does not type-check (the implicit conversion to the interface is lost). The fix rejects an interface parameter with a non-interface element (the check later generalized for golang/go#74938).

settings_note: The modernize analyzer is on by default in both builds; the reporter ran the modernize command, which runs the same analyzer.

files.source: issue body, 'What did you do?' code block

files.note: a module around the file (the reporter used go 1.24.2 and gives no go.mod); go 1.24 (slices needs go1.21)

repro.steps: Open main.go. The slicescontains pass reports the loop in IterateFruits ('Loop can be simplified using slices.ContainsFunc'). Apply its fix ('Replace loop by call to slices.ContainsFunc'). Reported: 'in call to slices.ContainsFunc, S (type []Fruit) does not satisfy ~[]E'. Probe: a fresh session on the edited text must report no error the original did not have; no fix offered means absent (the fix stops offering it).
